extracted.intended_audience: Sunday-school teachers, advanced catechism classes, priests, catechists, converts, and Catholic families
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and explanatory text for using The Baltimore Catechism (No. 4) as a teaching textbook: how teachers should present explanations, use examples, ask questions, and adapt the material for Sunday-school, advanced classes, adult instruction, and converts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended for the use of Sunday-school teachers and advanced classes; also useful for instruction of adults, converts, priests on missions, Catholic families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book is designed primarily as a teacher's aid for Sunday schools and advanced catechism classes but is explicitly recommended for adults, converts, mission priests with little time, and family use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and simplicity of explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations are to be full and simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language; avoid overly technical or controversial treatments; present doctrine in straightforward terms so teachers can read or paraphrase for pupils who cannot use longer controversial works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples should be taken from Holy Scripture, Our Lord's parables, incidents in His life, and the customs and manners of His time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make examples applicable to daily life through reflections and exhortations so pupils can relate doctrine to ordinary duties and experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, applied focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief aim is to be practical and to teach Catholics what they should know and how truths apply to everyday duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not primarily a devotional or controversial work, though it may cover those areas; emphasize application of doctrine to conduct and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular usability with or without explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Catechism is complete and distinct in itself and may be used with or without the explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers may use the bare questions/answers alone or add the explanations as time permits; explanations are optional supplements to the primary catechism text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom procedure for presenting explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: After hearing the lesson, the teacher is supposed to read the explanation of the new lesson as far as time will allow; explanation may be read as written or learned and given in substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the explanation aloud to the class or summarize it in the teacher's own words; adapt length to available class time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-memorization of explanations; active questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Children are not supposed to memorize the explanation as they do the Catechism itself; the teacher, having once read it, should ask questions on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the explanations as comprehension material rather than rote text; follow up with questions to ensure understanding and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary numbered questions for advanced instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete list of numbered questions on the explanations is provided at the end to render it serviceable as a textbook for more advanced classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appended question lists for higher-level classes or examination preparation; employ them to convert explanations into testable lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic repetition and cross-referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations may be repeated where the same subject occurs in different parts of the Catechism to show connection, reinforce memory, or save the teacher returning to previous pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition is intentional to (a) show conceptual links across lessons, (b) reinforce learning, and (c) make teaching more efficient by avoiding constant page-turning; use numbering and index to locate related explanations easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging format: interspersed Q&A
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations are interrupted by the questions and answers of the Catechism proper to increase readability and pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate explanatory prose with the Catechism's Q&A structure to maintain interest and facilitate classroom recitation and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for limited-contact instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to assist priests or teachers who can instruct converts or pupils only occasionally or for short periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials and explanations are concise and accessible enough to benefit learners who have infrequent contact with an instructor; prioritize essentials and clear examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The work aims to cover the truths of religion in a single, simple volume for teachers and families, addressing doctrine, morals, sacraments, prayers, and commandments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize material so that essential doctrines and moral teaching are accessible without needing multiple supplementary volumes; include indexes and lists of questions for navigation.
